title: Landing page copy or page brief

gates.text: Truth: no testimonial, name, rating, customer count, logo, press mention, statistic, guarantee or deadline that isn't in confirmed facts or cited research. Missing proof is marked [NEEDS FACT: ...]; no sample or illustrative quotes.
Structure: a hero with H1, subhead, one primary CTA (verb + outcome) and proof; one conversion goal for the page; a written thank-you step; a stated or explicitly assumed traffic source.

Compliance: no fake urgency or scarcity, no promised results the business can't guarantee, marketing consent (if collected) is a separate unticked checkbox with a privacy link, no unsourced superlatives.

anchors.1: H1 unrelated to the ad or email that sends traffic.
anchors.3: Same theme as the ad, but different words or offer.
anchors.5: The ad's key words, promise, offer and price repeated in H1 and subhead.

anchors.1: Clever or vague headline; offer buried.
anchors.3: Clear what it is, but who it's for or the price is buried.
anchors.5: What, who, price and next step instantly clear on a phone screen.

anchors.3: Generic testimonials or proof grouped far from claims.
anchors.5: Specific, attributed, numeric proof beside each claim; strongest proof in the hero.

anchors.3: Generic FAQ not drawn from VOC.
anchors.5: Top 3–5 VOC objections each answered where they arise, with concrete reducers (trial, guarantee, import help, named person).

anchors.1: Long form, several competing CTAs, unclear next step.
anchors.3: Reasonable form; some unneeded fields or vague button text.
anchors.5: Minimum justified fields, visible labels, outcome button, friction-removing micro-copy, one action, clear thank-you step.

anchors.1: Order ignores the reader (e.g. long problem section for brand-search traffic, offer-first for cold traffic).
anchors.3: Standard template applied without adjusting for awareness or price.
anchors.5: Opening, order and length chosen from the awareness level and commitment, with the reasoning visible in the brief.

anchors.1: Jargon, hype, AI tells, long dense paragraphs.
anchors.5: Grade 5–8 (consumer), paragraphs of 3 lines or fewer, descriptive subheads, 'you' leads, VOC phrases, sounds like this business.
Prices, times, places, process and names throughout; fails the competitor swap test.

anchors.1: No visual, mobile or measurement guidance.
anchors.5: Real visuals listed, mobile CTA and tap targets, speed flagged, conversion event named, one big-swing test proposed.
